extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Common birds and body parts — sparrow, crow, parrot, pigeon, eagle are common Indian birds. Body parts: head, eyes, beak, wings, feathers, tail, legs, claws. (2) How birds fly — birds have hollow bones (light body), wings (push air), feathers (help glide), strong chest muscles (power wing beats), streamlined body (cuts through air). Birds flap wings to push air down and lift up. (3) Bird food habits and beak adaptation — beak shape matches food: short thick beak = seeds (sparrow), hooked sharp beak = meat/fish (eagle), curved strong beak = fruits (parrot), long chisel beak = insects in bark (woodpecker), broad flat beak = filtering water (duck). (4) Bird nests and habitats — nests are for laying eggs and raising chicks, not for sleeping. Different birds build different nests: sparrow (twigs on tree), pigeon (buildings/ledges), weaver bird (hanging woven nest), eagle (large nest on cliffs), duck (near water). Misconceptions: 'birds live in nests all the time' (birds use nests only for breeding, not for sleeping every night), 'all birds eat the same food' (beak shape determines food type), 'penguins and ostriches are common Indian birds' (they are not found in India — penguins live in Antarctica, ostriches in Africa), 'feathers are only for flying' (feathers also keep birds warm and waterproof).
